embedding_text:
CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?

Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. CJC-1295 is not FDA-approved for anti-aging, muscle building, or fat loss. #CJC1295 #Peptides #GrowthHormone #PeptideResearch #IGF1 ⚠️ DISCLAIMER This video is for educational purposes only. TB-500 is finally entering human research. 🧬

TB-500 has been discussed for years in the peptide and biohacking communities for its potential role in recovery, tissue repair and healing. But there's an important catch: much of the excitement surrounding TB-500 has been based on preclinical research, animal studies, and research involving its parent molecule, thymosin beta-4—not robust human clinical evidence for TB-500 itself. Now that's beginning to change. A human clinical trial involving TB-500 is giving researchers an opportunity to start answering the questions that matter: What happens in humans? GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?

GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. embedding_text:
GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?

Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?

Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?

GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. embedding_text:
GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. That raises a much bigger question for the future of GLP-1 treatment: Could people eventually lose weight with weekly injections, then transition to one injection a month for maintenance? In this video, we break down how VK2735 works, GLP-1 + GIP signaling, the new maintenance data, side effects, limitations of the study, and why the next generation of obesity drugs may compete not only on how much weight people lose — but how rarely they need to take the medication. One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. BPC-157 Is EXPLODING — New Data Shows a 33X Surge

BPC-157 use appears to be exploding. New 2026 research found a 33-fold increase in newly documented BPC-157 users, rising from just 4 in the first quarter of 2020 to 134 in the first quarter of 2026 within a large medical-record network. But the most surprising number may be 79%. Among BPC-157 users whose medical records contained a clear outcome, about 79% had improvement documented. Does that mean BPC-157 actually works? Not so fast. It's one of the most interesting looks yet at how this controversial peptide is being used in the real world. But there's an important distinction between popularity and proof. The study was observational, had no placebo group, did not use a standardized BPC-157 dose or treatment period, and many patients were using other therapies at the same time. GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Not Every Biohack Is Worth Trying

🚫 Not Every Biohack Deserves a Try When Dr. Kevin White was asked about biohacks that seem crazy or need more research, he had a very clear example: drinking urine. He shared that he had heard of patients practicing urine drinking and questioned the reasoning behind it. His response was simple: just because something is labeled a “biohack” doesn’t mean it should automatically be considered a wellness strategy. The broader lesson is worth remembering in a world full of viral health trends: 🔬 Question the claim. 📚 Look for credible evidence. 🩺 Consider safety before experimenting. Not every unconventional practice deserves a place in your health routine. Sometimes, the smartest approach is knowing when to say no and move on. #Biohacking #HealthTrends #HealthEducation #Wellness #HealthyLiving #HealthOptimization #CriticalThinking #EvidenceBasedHealth #Longevity #BiohackingCommunity #WellnessJourney #HealthyHabits

Dr. Jeff Gross’s Favorite Wearable

⌚ Dr. Jeff Gross’s Favorite Wearable: Why He Keeps Coming Back to Apple Watch Dr. Jeff Gross says he enjoys experimenting with different wearable devices, from smartwatches and rings to newer health-tracking technologies. Right now, he’s testing several options, including a new smart ring and a blood-pressure monitoring watch. He also wears an EMF-blocking device, although he openly acknowledges that he isn’t sure whether it actually works. But despite trying new technology, one device continues to stand out for him: the Apple Watch. 🍎⌚ One feature he particularly values is heart rate variability (HRV) tracking, which he considers an important metric for understanding aspects of his health and recovery. His approach highlights the rapidly evolving world of wearable technology: keep experimenting, learn what the data can tell you, and stay curious about new tools. 💡 The best wearable may not be the newest one—it may be the one that gives you useful information you can actually understand and use. #AppleWatch #WearableTechnology #HRV #HeartRateVariability #HealthTracking #FitnessTracking #Biohacking #HealthOptimization #Wellness #Recovery #Longevity #HealthTech

GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. GLP-1 Once a Month?! New VK2735 Results Could Change Weight Loss

What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Participants first lost weight using weekly VK2735. Researchers then tested whether less-frequent dosing could help maintain those results. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. In the study, participants first received weekly VK2735 and lost approximately 16% to 19% of their body weight after 21 weeks. Researchers then tested less-frequent maintenance dosing. The results were fascinating: 💉 Every-other-week dosing maintained up to 97% of previous weight loss 📅 Once-monthly dosing maintained up to 90% ⚖️ Participants switched to placebo maintained about 61% 📉 A small weekly-treatment group reached an average 21.7% weight loss after 33 weeks But there's an important distinction: this does not mean people started with a once-a-month injection and lost 20% of their body weight. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. What if you didn't have to take a GLP-1 every week — but only once a month? New clinical trial results for VK2735, an experimental GLP-1/GIP drug from Viking Therapeutics, suggest that less-frequent dosing could eventually play a role in maintaining weight loss. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav

“The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. They Lab Tested Retatrutide — The Results Were Shocking

Are you actually getting the peptide you paid for? In this Peptide A to Z investigation, we look at independent laboratory testing of peptide products labeled Retatrutide and NAD+ that were purchased over the counter from a Brooklyn smoke shop. Four sealed vials were tested. Two were labeled Retatrutide 10mg. Two were labeled NAD+ 500mg. 🧬 FREE PEPTIDE GUIDE: Get the Peptide A to Z Guide and learn the basics of peptides, research, terminology, and more: PeptideAtoZ.com 👥 JOIN THE PEPTIDE A TO Z COMMUNITY: Connect with others interested in peptide research, longevity, and the latest peptide science: PeptideAtoZ.com According to the reported laboratory results, none of the four samples could be positively identified as the substance stated on the label. The retatrutide samples also produced an unexpected signal that the laboratory described as suggesting “extreme contamination.” But the story gets even more concerning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. “The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. YOUNGER: Pellets, Peptides Patient Care with Matthew Moody, NP

“I provide patient directed care. If you are my patient, you will be my absolute focus. I will listen, examine you, and together we will discover the root cause of the issue, and begin to take an optimal plan of action. “ ---Matthew Moody Nurse Practitioner (NP) New Provider at Santa Fe Soul (SFS) Center for Regenerative Medicine https://santafesoul.com/meet-our-providers/ YOUNGER Podcast Episode Summary: Have you ever heard of peptides or pellets? Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav

“The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. YOUNGER: The Seat of the Soul with Gary Zukav

“The choice that frees or imprisons us is the choice of love or fear. Love liberates. Fear imprisons “. -- Gary Zukav, Spiritual Teacher and New York Times Bestselling Author. Gary Zukav (born October 17, 1942) is an American spiritual teacher, and the author of four consecutive New York Times Best Sellers. Beginning in 1998, he appeared more than 30 times on The Oprah Winfrey Show to discuss transformation in human consciousness which were concepts he presented in his book, The Seat of the Soul. Gary’s first book, The Dancing Wu Li Masters (1979), won a U.S. National Book Award. It is an overview of the New Physics, and became the winner of The American Book Award for Science. Gary’s book The Seat of the Soul, was celebrated as a #1 New York Times Bestseller for three consecutive years in a row. His book, Soul Stories, was also a New York Times bestselling book; and many other books he has written that followed. Gary’s books have sold millions of copies and are published in twenty-four languages. He is a graduate of Harvard University and a former U.S. Army Special Forces (Green Beret) officer with Vietnam service. Gary lives in Oregon. Linda Francis was his spiritual partner for decades. She passed on in 2022, and Gary has said, “She (Linda) was a model to me and many others.” Dr. Robyn Benson's next YOUNGER podcast episode is an interview with "The Seat of the Soul" New York Times Bestselling Author, Gary Zukav. Watch, listen and learn from this powerful, timely video…

Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Orexin Explained: The Peptide That Keeps Your Brain Awake

What if one tiny peptide system in your brain helps determine whether you stay awake or fall asleep? In this episode of Peptide A to Z, we break down orexin, a naturally occurring peptide system that plays a major role in wakefulness, alertness, sleep, and narcolepsy. People with narcolepsy type 1 lose most of the brain cells that produce orexin. Without enough orexin signaling, the brain can struggle to maintain the normal boundary between being awake and asleep—leading to severe daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, and other symptoms. But in 2026, the orexin story reached a major milestone. We explore how researchers developed a new approach that targets the orexin 2 receptor, why this is fundamentally different from simply using a stimulant, and how the same peptide system can actually be targeted in the opposite direction to help treat insomnia. In this video: • What orexin A and orexin B are • How orexin helps keep the brain awake • The connection between orexin and narcolepsy type 1 • What cataplexy is • The 2026 breakthrough in orexin-targeted treatment • Why blocking orexin can help people sleep • Orexin's potential roles in appetite, motivation, reward, stress, and metabolism • Why this peptide system could become increasingly important in medicine One peptide system. Turn it down to help people sleep. Turn it up to help people stay awake. Subscribe to Peptide A to Z for straightforward breakdowns of peptide research, clinical studies, and emerging…

The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s

Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Glucagon Explained: The Peptide Behind Retatrutide’s Secret Weapon

What if one of the most important peptides in your body does almost the OPPOSITE of insulin? It's called glucagon. Insulin helps lower blood sugar. Glucagon can help raise it — and it's so powerful that glucagon is used as an emergency medicine for severe low blood sugar. But that's only part of the story. Scientists are now targeting the glucagon system alongside GLP-1 and GIP in retatrutide, an experimental triple-receptor agonist producing remarkable results in human trials. In this video, we break down: What glucagon is and how it works Why glucagon can raise blood sugar How glucagon differs from insulin Why glucagon is an established medicine Why scientists would target glucagon for weight loss How retatrutide targets GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon The human evidence behind retatrutide Why “glucagon is the opposite of insulin” is useful — but an oversimplification In a Phase 2 trial, the highest retatrutide dose produced 24.2% average weight loss at 48 weeks. More recently, Lilly reported 28.3% average weight loss at 80 weeks at the highest dose in its Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 trial. Retatrutide remains investigational and is not currently FDA approved. 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research. Education. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research. Your Gut Is Talking to Your Brain: Here’s What It’s Saying

Your gut isn't just digesting food. It's talking to your brain constantly, through the vagus nerve, through neurotransmitters, through inflammation signals that shape mood, focus, and stress response. Your oral microbiome is doing its own signaling too. Research links oral bacteria to cardiovascular health, since certain strains can enter the bloodstream and contribute to arterial inflammation. Gut and oral health are highly individual. What heals one person's gut can quietly feed the wrong bacteria in someone else's. Generic advice like "eat more fiber" or "take a probiotic" often misses the mark because it isn't built around your specific microbiome. Viome tests your gut and oral microbiome directly, then gives you a personalized breakdown of which foods to eat, which to avoid, and which supplements actually match your biology.

What if one of the most important peptides in your body does almost the OPPOSITE of insulin? It's called glucagon. Insulin helps lower blood sugar. Glucagon can help raise it — and it's so powerful that glucagon is used as an emergency medicine for severe low blood sugar. But that's only part of the story. Scientists are now targeting the glucagon system alongside GLP-1 and GIP in retatrutide, an experimental triple-receptor agonist producing remarkable results in human trials. More recently, Lilly reported 28.3% average weight loss at 80 weeks at the highest dose in its Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 trial. The Peptide That Actually Builds Bone? 65% Lower Fracture Risk

Can a peptide actually BUILD new bone? Forteo, also known as teriparatide, is an FDA-approved peptide medicine with something most peptides discussed online don't have: large human trials and evidence showing fewer fractures. In this video, we break down how Forteo works, why it can stimulate new bone formation, and the major human trial where the standard dose was associated with about a 65% lower relative risk of new spinal fractures compared with placebo. We also look at one of the most fascinating parts of its history: early animal studies raised concerns about bone tumors, Forteo originally carried an FDA boxed warning, and years of human safety evidence eventually led the FDA to remove that boxed warning. This is a perfect example of why the question isn't simply “Do peptides work?” The better question is: Which peptide, for what purpose, and where is the human evidence? 📘 FREE Peptide Guide: PeptideAtoZ.com/free-guide 💬 Join the Peptide A to Z Community: PeptideAtoZ.com/community 🔬 Peptide A to Z Research.
